findings.text: No test covers If-Match (or a star If-Match) when the response has no ETag, nor a failing If-Match combined with If-None-Match, so the ordering of the 412 check before the 304 check is unproven.
The `if_none_match.star_tag` and `if_match.star_tag` branches could be folded into a small helper, but this is cosmetic.

coverage.note: Precedence tests, per-method If-Match tests and the no_headers Accept-Ranges assertion together cover the RFC order and the header.
412 on unsafe methods, 304 on GET/HEAD, and the entity headers removed from the 304 are each asserted.
Star ETag is tested with exists True and False for both If-Match and If-None-Match, with different outcomes.
The non-GET, non-200, unknown/zero length and non-bytes unit cases are each tested, and each asserts Accept-Ranges.
First-range-only, clamping, suffix, unsatisfiable and basic 206 are all asserted, including Content-Length, Content-Range and data.
Matching, mismatching and weak ETags are tested, plus the date match and mismatch in the sibling test.
